title: OAuth tokens are persisted in the integrations collection as plaintext, despite an unused AES-256-GCM utility being available
description: ConnectorService.handleOAuthCallback() (ConnectorService.ts:1047-1054, comment reads 'Store tokens directly in Integration credentials (plain, matching backend schema)') writes accessToken/refreshToken straight into credentials.* via integrationRepo.updateOAuthTokens(). SyncService's updateOAuthTokens (ConnectorConfigRepository.ts:334-365) does the same on refresh. src/utils/crypto.ts exports encryptCredentials()/decryptCredentials() (AES-256-GCM, iv:authTag:ciphertext format) but a repo-wide search found zero call sites for either function outside crypto.ts itself — the encryption utility is dead code. This is a genuine at-rest storage gap, not a hypothetical.
preconditions: DB access (or a Mongo export) for the integrations collection in a non-prod environment
An OAuth-based connector (e.g. Google Drive, GitHub, Okta, Jira) has completed its connect flow
steps: Complete the OAuth connect flow for any OAuth connector
Query the integrations collection directly for that document's credentials field
expectedResult: Current behavior (gap): accessToken/refreshToken are stored as readable plaintext strings, not as the iv:authTag:ciphertext format produced by encryptCredentials(). This should be flagged for remediation — wire encryptCredentials()/decryptCredentials() into the write/read path (ConnectorConfigRepository) so credentials are encrypted at rest, matching the masking already applied on read via getConnector().

title: OAuth callback rejects a state parameter that does not exist in Redis (expired, forged, or already-consumed)
description: handleOAuthCallback() looks up oauth-state:<state> in Redis; if stateData is null it returns 400 'OAuth state not found or expired.' The key is deleted immediately after a successful exchange (ConnectorService.ts:1108-1109), so replaying the same callback URL a second time must also fail this check.
preconditions: A completed OAuth connect flow for any connector
steps: Complete an OAuth connect flow for a connector end to end
Copy the exact callback URL (with its code and state query params) used for that completed flow
Replay the same callback URL a second time
expectedResult: The replayed callback is rejected with 400 'OAuth state not found or expired. Please restart the OAuth flow.' — the state key was already deleted on first use, so no second token exchange or credential overwrite occurs.

title: GET /connectors/:id returns 404 for a connector ID belonging to another organization
description: ConnectorService.getConnector() calls integrationRepo.findById(integrationId, orgId) with the requesting user's organizationIdString — an org-scoped lookup, not a bare _id lookup. A cross-org ID must not leak even a 403-with-metadata response.
preconditions: Two organizations (A, B), each with at least one connector configured
Valid JWT for a user in org A with integration.read/INTEGRATION_HUB VIEW permission
steps: As an org A user, call GET /connectors/:id using a connector ID that belongs to org B
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 404 'Integration not found.' — no connector name, type, masked credentials, or accountInfo belonging to org B is returned in the response body.

title: MANAGE_CONNECTORS-only routes (create, update, delete, test-connection) reject a user who only holds VIEW permission
description: connector.routes.ts gates DELETE /connectors/:id, POST /connectors/:id/test, and the create/update routes behind requirePermission(INTEGRATION_HUB_PERMISSIONS.MANAGE_CONNECTORS), a stricter permission than the VIEW-gated GET routes. A viewer-role user must not be able to disconnect or reconfigure an integration.
preconditions: A user whose role grants INTEGRATION_HUB VIEW but not MANAGE_CONNECTORS
steps: As the VIEW-only user, call GET /connectors (should succeed)
As the same user, call DELETE /connectors/:id for an existing connector
As the same user, call POST /connectors/:id/test
expectedResult: The GET call succeeds (200). The DELETE and test-connection calls are both rejected with 403 — the connector is not disabled and no live connection test is executed against the third-party service.

title: Webhook receiver rejects a payload signed with the wrong organization's webhook secret
description: POST /webhooks/:connectorType reads credentials.webhookSecret from the matched integration record and calls verifyWebhookSignature(). If an attacker who knows org B's webhook secret targets org A's webhook URL/connector, the signature computed against org A's stored secret must not validate.
preconditions: Two orgs each have a GitHub (or Jira) integration configured with distinct webhookSecret values
steps: Compute a valid HMAC signature for a sample payload using org B's webhookSecret
POST that payload to org A's webhook endpoint with the org-B-signed header
expectedResult: Signature verification fails; the request is rejected before the payload is enqueued to the evidence-webhook queue, and no evidence is created or attributed to org A from a payload it did not actually send.

title: No integrations frontend component persists access tokens, refresh tokens, or client secrets to localStorage/sessionStorage
description: Regression guard: a repo-wide search of vibrantix-client-panel/src for localStorage/sessionStorage usage inside integrations-related files (AllIntegrationsContent.jsx, integrationHubService.js, integrationService.js, IntegrationsCatalog.jsx, GoogleDriveIntegrationCard.js, GitHubIntegrationPage.jsx, AWSIntegrationConfigModal.jsx, OktaIntegrationPage.jsx) currently returns zero matches — credential values only ever pass through getConnector()'s already-masked response. This case locks in that property so a future change doesn't introduce client-side token persistence.
steps: Open browser DevTools on /integrations and complete an OAuth connect flow for any connector
Inspect Application > Local Storage and Session Storage for the app origin
Inspect the React DevTools component tree / Redux state for any card or modal that rendered credential fields
expectedResult: No accessToken, refreshToken, apiKey, or client secret value appears in localStorage, sessionStorage, or persisted client state at any point — only the masked (`****xyz9`-style) representation from the API is ever rendered or held in memory.

title: Disconnecting an integration soft-deletes the local record but does not call the provider's OAuth token-revocation endpoint
description: ConnectorService.deleteConnector() (ConnectorService.ts:504-554) sets the integration to inactive via integrationRepo.softDelete(), deactivates linked AWS accounts if applicable, invalidates Redis cache, and writes an audit log entry — but it never calls the third-party provider's revoke endpoint (e.g. Google's oauth2.revoke, GitHub's token deletion API). The access/refresh token therefore remains valid at the provider until it naturally expires, even though Vibrantix will no longer use it.
preconditions: An active Google Drive (or other OAuth) integration with a valid, unexpired access token
steps: Note the current access token value for the integration (via a debug/inspection path, not production UI)
Disconnect the integration from the Integration Hub
Attempt to use the same token directly against the provider's API (e.g. Google Drive files.list) outside of Vibrantix
expectedResult: Current behavior (gap): the integration shows as disconnected/inactive in Vibrantix and Vibrantix itself no longer uses the token, but the token is still accepted by the provider's API until its natural expiry — no server-side revocation call is made. Flag for remediation: call the provider's revoke endpoint in deleteConnector() before/alongside the soft delete.
